title: Omniscient God, 'Tis Thine to Know
description: Omniscient God, 'Tis Thine to Know in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 398 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Charitable Judgment”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Om-ni-scient God, 'tis thine to know The springs whence wrong o-pin-ions flow; To judge from prin-ci-ples with-in, When frail-ty errs, and when we sin.

lines: The springs whence wrong opinions flow;
When frailty errs, and when we sin.
Who with another's eye can read,
We humbly seek and use our own.
If wrong, forgive; accept, if right,
Whilst faithful, we obey our light,
And judging none, are zealous still
To follow, as to learn, thy will.
When shall our happy eyes behold
Thy people, fashioned in thy mould?
Derived from thee, O God of love?
